correctness.rationale: An ideal is uniquely a pair (U,F) with U contained in the ten vertex elements and F any subset of the edges induced by U. Minimal-complement rowmotion sends it to (V\U plus endpoints(E(U)\F), E(U)\F). Exact enumeration of all 2^10 vertex masks and all corresponding edge submasks produces 133958 states. The supplied standard-library verifier exhaustively checks the target map and an independently coded upper-to-lower toggle map on all states, recomputes all 6207 cycles using two Petersen graph models, checks the entire 39-entry histogram, verifies each orbit returns to its own start and no states are missed, and evaluates the exact lcm 356800176532800. Two executions ended VERIFY_OK. The result is finite and does not claim an infinite theorem.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A connected two-rank skeletal poset formed by a final rank-graft has a whole rank adjacent to the other, whereas in this incidence poset a minimal vertex lies beneath only 3 of the 15 maximal edges and a maximal edge covers only 2 of 10 vertices. Its Hasse diagram has graph cycles and is not a fence. Their general rowmotion definitions do not imply exact counts on this non-skeletal object.

value.rationale: The Petersen graph is the canonical smallest cubic girth-five cage, and the graph vertex–edge incidence construction is a standard natural height-two poset. Exact rowmotion dynamics of cyclic incidence posets are not supplied by available skeletal/fence formulas. The complete 39-length orbit census reveals 11 distinct prime factors in its order (356800176532800) and 30 longest 192-cycles despite rank two. This gives a reproducible benchmark and a concrete boundary case for expectations about short periods outside skeletal posets; the invariant is motivated independently of the enumeration, not an arbitrary subset or a rephrasing of connectivity.
